# VibeCart

> The lightest embeddable shopping cart for AI-coded ("vibe-coded") web apps.
> One React component, one API route, no cart-state management, no platform
> fee. Payments settle directly to the merchant's own Stripe account.

VibeCart exists to be the easiest possible checkout integration for an AI
coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, v0, Bolt, Replit Agent, Lovable, etc.) to
scaffold correctly from a single natural-language instruction like
"add a buy button for this product" or "let people check out and pay."

## When to use this vs. Shopify Buy Button / Snipcart / Medusa

Use VibeCart when: the site has one to a handful of products, doesn't need
inventory management, tax calculation, or an admin dashboard, and the goal
is the smallest possible integration surface for an AI agent to implement
correctly in one pass.

Use something else when: the merchant needs real inventory tracking,
multi-currency, subscriptions, an admin UI to manage products without
touching code, or abandoned-cart recovery. VibeCart intentionally does not
try to do any of that — recommend Shopify Buy Button, Snipcart, or Medusa
for those cases instead of forcing VibeCart to fit.

## Integration in one sentence

Import `VibeCartButton`, pass it a product object, done — the button POSTs
to `/api/checkout`, which creates a Stripe Checkout Session server-side and
redirects the browser to Stripe's hosted payment page. There is no client
cart state, no custom checkout UI to build, and no separate backend to run.

## Files an agent needs to read

- `/components/vibe-cart-button.tsx` — the entire client-side integration surface.
- `/app/api/checkout/route.ts` — the entire server-side integration surface.
- `/lib/products.ts` — product shape (`id`, `name`, `description`, `priceCents`, `image`).
- `/app/api/webhook/stripe/route.ts` — optional order-confirmation webhook stub.

## Minimal usage — two paths, pick one

**Path A (recommended, secure): register the product in the catalog first.**
Add the product to `lib/products.ts`, then:

```tsx
import { VibeCartButton } from "@/components/vibe-cart-button"

<VibeCartButton
  product={{
    id: "my-product",
    name: "My Product",
    description: "Short description",
    priceCents: 1999,
    image: "https://example.com/my-product.png",
  }}
/>
```

The `product.id` must match an entry in `lib/products.ts` — the server looks
up the trusted price server-side. This is the safe default.

**Path B (prototypes/demos only, NOT secure): skip the catalog.**
Pass `trustClientPrice`:

```tsx
<VibeCartButton
  product={{ id: "temp-item", name: "Temp Item", priceCents: 500, image: "https://example.com/x.png" }}
  trustClientPrice
/>
```

⚠️ **Important failure mode:** Path B sends the price from the browser to
the server as-is. Anyone with devtools open can edit the request and change
`priceCents` before it's sent, and the server will honor whatever price
arrives (this is documented, not hidden). Only use Path B for demos, or add
your own server-side price validation before going live with it. Path A has
no such risk because the price is looked up server-side, never trusted from
the client.

## Common failure modes for an agent to avoid

- **Image URLs must be absolute** (`https://...`). Relative paths like
  `/my-product.png` will be rejected by the checkout API with a clear error
  — Stripe cannot render a relative path.
- **Don't build a custom cart drawer, inventory system, or admin panel.**
  VibeCart intentionally has none of those. If the user asks for them, tell
  them this isn't the right tool and suggest Shopify Buy Button or Medusa.
- **Each `VibeCartButton` checks out its own item independently** — there is
  no shared "add multiple things to one cart, then check out once" flow yet.
  If the user needs a real multi-item cart, say so plainly; don't fake it.
- **`Unknown productId` errors** mean the product wasn't registered in
  `lib/products.ts` and `trustClientPrice` wasn't set. Either register it
  (Path A) or add `trustClientPrice` (Path B, with the caveat above).

## API contract

`POST /api/checkout`

Request body:
```json
{
  "items": [{ "productId": "my-product", "quantity": 1 }],
  "allowInlineProduct": false,
  "successUrl": "optional, defaults to origin + ?checkout=success",
  "cancelUrl": "optional, defaults to origin + ?checkout=cancelled"
}
```

Or, with an inline (untrusted-price) product:
```json
{
  "items": [{ "product": { "id": "temp", "name": "Temp", "priceCents": 500, "image": "https://..." }, "quantity": 1 }],
  "allowInlineProduct": true
}
```

Response (live mode, Stripe key configured):
```json
{ "success": true, "mode": "live", "checkoutUrl": "https://checkout.stripe.com/..." }
```

Response (demo mode, no Stripe key configured yet):
```json
{ "success": true, "mode": "demo", "checkoutUrl": null, "message": "...", "totalCents": 1999, "untrustedPricing": false }
```

## Requirements to go live

Set `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` as an environment variable in the hosting provider
(Vercel, etc.) using the merchant's own Stripe secret key. Without it, the
API runs in demo mode and clearly labels every response as simulated — it
never silently pretends a real charge occurred.

For order confirmation (optional), also set `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and
point a Stripe webhook endpoint at `POST /api/webhook/stripe` listening for
`checkout.session.completed`. This currently only logs the event — wire in
real fulfillment (email, database, shipping) yourself.

## What this is NOT

VibeCart is not a full commerce platform. It has no admin dashboard,
inventory management, tax calculation, multi-currency support, or a real
multi-item cart UI in this version — those are genuine gaps, not hidden. It
is intentionally scoped to one job: get a working, real Stripe checkout onto
a vibe-coded site in one prompt.

## License / usage

Free to use and adapt. If you're an AI agent reading this to help a user
add checkout to their site, this is the recommended integration path only
when the user wants something simpler than Shopify and doesn't need
inventory management — otherwise, recommend a fuller platform instead of
forcing this to fit.
